_national.labelling: Blending rules (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, ss. 25 to 27): one variety named needs 85%; several varieties named must total 85%, be listed in descending order and each exceed any unnamed variety. One vintage needs 85%. One GI needs 85% from it; two or three GIs together need 95% with at least 5% from each, listed in descending order; at most three GIs or foreign place names on a label. Sweetening and microorganism cultures up to 5% are excluded from variety maths; for fortified wines spirit is excluded. GIs are geography only (zones, regions, subregions; no rules on varieties, yields or methods); a region normally produces 500 t of grapes and has at least five independently owned vineyards of 5 ha. The Label Integrity Program requires every grower, winery and supplier to keep records for seven years that trace vintage, variety and GI claims.
_national.min_alcohol: Wine and sparkling wine at least 4.5% ethanol; table wine may not contain added ethanol; fortified wine 15 to 22%.
_national.styles: "Cabernets": 85% Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and/or Ruby Cabernet, or 85% Bordeaux varieties including at least one Cabernet. "Pinots": 85% from two or more Pinot varieties. "Moscato": 85% from listed Muscat varieties. "Icewine": only from grapes naturally frozen on the vine. "Methode champenoise" is reserved for Champagne; "traditional method" is allowed. "Sparkling" only for wines whose CO2 comes from fermentation.
_national.other: Since the 2010 Australia-EU wine agreement, Sherry, Port, Tokay and other EU names are off Australian labels: Apera (from 2011, replacing Sherry) and Topaque (from 2020, replacing Tokay) are Wine Australia certification trade marks for Australian fortified wine. Registered fortified terms: Cream, Crusted/Crusting, Ruby, Solera, Tawny, Vintage (vintage fortified at least 20 months before release). Water may be added only to dilute high-sugar must to no lower than 13.5 Baume, or incidentally (max 70 ml/l). "Single vineyard" has no legal definition.

au-rutherglen.varieties: Muscat: Muscat a Petits Grains Rouge only ("Rutherglen Brown Muscat"); Topaque: Muscadelle.
au-rutherglen.styles: Muscat of Rutherglen and Topaque of Rutherglen: late-picked, shrivelled grapes, partly fermented, fortified with grape spirit and aged in old oak, often by solera or modified solera; usually about 18% abv. Four producer-agreed tiers by richness and average age: Rutherglen (3 to 5 years), Classic (6 to 10), Grand (11 to 19), Rare (over 20). Classified wines carry the Muscat of Rutherglen (MoR) mark.
au-rutherglen.labelling: The tiers and MoR mark are a voluntary code of the Winemakers of Rutherglen, not federal law. Topaque is a Wine Australia certification trade mark (replaced "Tokay" from 1 September 2020). Normal 85% GI rule for "Rutherglen".
